newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end up, snapping 5-day losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end up, snapping 5-day losing streak.

text.p: Volatile Indian stocks reversed a five-day losing streak in choppy trade on Thursday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to end higher, but brokers said the market might face some resistance before notching further gains.
The Bombay index closed 11.88 points, or 0.28-percent higher, at a provisional 4,195.30 to recoup some of the five-percent fall registered in the past five sessions.
"What has happened is that the market went into a corrective phase (lower)," Jaspreet Ahuja, head of sales at Caspian Research said. "But people are definitely waiting to accumulate at these levels."
Bombay blue chips fell sharply on profit-taking after crossing 33-month highs last week at 4,448.06.
"Foreign fund buying was halted due to political worries," said Bharat Iyer, strategist at UBS Securities.
Regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party planned earlier this week to pull-out from the ruling coalition.

But the DMK party said it would continue to support the government from the outside. Four of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ministers are part of the DMK including industry minister Murasoli M"The market had also been overbought," Iyer said.

Traders said a crucial core committee meeting of the 15-party United Front government on Thursday evening to thrash out nagging issues rocking the three-month old government would provide cues to share prices.
But some traders said politics was just an excuse for the correction.
"The market had also been overbought," Iyer said.
Now, Iyer said "the reason why the markets are doing well has got to do with liquidity. There is so much cash surplus available that money has to find its way into equities."

Traders expected continued buying by U.S.-based funds, which have largely contributed to the 35-percent jump in Indian stocks in 1997 amid a surging Dow, would take prices to even higher levels with only minor hiccups on the way.

"With the Dow searing new records each day, U.S.-based foreign institutional investors (FII's) are likely to park (some) of their big profits into India," said a dealer at a U.S. based foreign brokerage.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average shattered the 8,000 mark on Wednesday after strong corporate profits and mild inflation data combined to trigger a buying frenzy.
U.S. stocks have soared nearly 25 percent in 1997 with help from solid corporate earnings growth and robust economic data.
Analysts said rising foreign portfolio funds in Indian equities was likely to take the Bombay index past its all-time high of 4,643.31, scored on September 12, 1994.
The strong fund inflows have made India the best performing Asian emerging markets in 1997.
Net foreign institutional investments were $57 million from July 1-9 after $362.9 million in June.
"I would look at an upside of 4,500 and a downside of 4,000. That's the range we are talking about," Caspian's Ahuja said.
Immediate support was seen near 4,1450, a level where fund buying could emerge, traders said.
